title: Moving Out of a Slice
goal: Learn why slice elements cannot be moved out and how in-place methods work.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Morning: Slices and Borrowing

sections.text: In languages like Python or C++, swapping two list elements uses a temporary variable. In Rust, elements behind a slice reference cannot be moved out.

sections.caption: Borrow the element instead of moving it.

sections.text: Moving an element out of a slice would leave uninitialized memory in the underlying collection. Rust stops this at compile time with error `E0507`.
If elements implement `Copy`, indexing copies them automatically. For owned types like `String`, you must borrow or use in-place slice methods.
Methods like `swap`, `reverse`, and `sort` operate on `&mut [T]` directly. They modify existing memory in place without allocating or moving items out.

explanation: Learn why slice elements cannot be moved out and how in-place methods work.
